first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in costa rica' on the train. Straight yes in the first lines, dated November 2026, and the Key Takeaways actually have numbers this time: 4 to 6 months, 25 working days. Good. But then I read 'you present yourselves together and both sign the request' and now I don't know if we have to fly to Costa Rica twice. That's the thing I'd want answered and the page says to ask. Then I jumped to the FAQ for the beach and the cost, and got 'ask the notary' and 'fees apply'. Bookmarked for the document list, not much more.

journey.quote: Costa Rica is on your shortlist, and before you choose a coast or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: Answer in line two. No fluff. Good.

journey.quote: This guide takes each step in the order you will meet it, as at November 2026, from the papers you gather at home to the certificate you carry back to Australia.
journey.reaction: Dated, so I know it's current. But it's all about Australia again. I'm in Singapore. Do the Costa Rica steps apply to me too? Probably, it says 'foreign applicants', but I have to work that out myself.

journey.quote: The Registro Civil route takes 4 to 6 months on average once your request is complete and your marriage notice has run in the official gazette, La Gaceta.
journey.reaction: A real number in the takeaways. That's the screenshot. Also a bit of a shock, 4 to 6 months is long.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Costa Rica at level 2, "Exercise a high degree of caution", due to the threat of violent crime, and notes that carjackings and "express kidnappings" are increasingly common.
journey.reaction: Whoa. First thing under the heading is kidnappings. Fair to say it, but then five paragraphs of visas, transit, departure tax and consulates before I reach the document list. Scrolled.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Read the full [Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/americas/costa-rica) before you book,.
journey.reaction: Stray comma before the full stop. Small, but it looks unedited.

journey.section: The documents you gather at home
journey.quote: That one-month window shapes your timeline more than anything else on the list, so order this certificate last.
journey.reaction: This is the useful bit. A real tip, not just a list. Would screenshot.

journey.quote: You then present yourselves together and both sign the request.
journey.reaction: Wait. In person? Months before the wedding? So we fly there twice? The heading says 'Sending your details ahead', which made me think we could do it from home. Then it says to ask the Unidad de Matrimonios. That's the biggest question on the page and it's left open.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, in the rainforest or at your resort
journey.quote: If you picture vows on a headland lawn or under a rainforest canopy, the setting rests on your notary, or on a symbolic ceremony after the legal signing.
journey.reaction: So the Registro Civil is office only, and the beach depends on the notary. Clearer than most pages, but still 'ask'. At least I know which route to look at.

journey.quote: For a wedding of this scale, the questions to put to a resort are less about the view and more about control.
journey.reaction: What scale? Nothing before this mentions a size. Then it asks about 'our private security'. I don't have private security. This section isn't written for me.

journey.quote: There is no charge for the registry service of celebrating a civil marriage before the Registro Civil.
journey.reaction: Free at the registry, nice to know. But then 'each carry their own fees' with no numbers. Just tell me roughly how much.

journey.quote: Yes. Your apostilled birth certificate and civil status certificate each need an official Spanish translation.
journey.reaction: Direct yes and what to do. That's how every FAQ answer should read.

journey.section: Plan your Costa Rica wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Australian company, fine. Not for me right now.

turn_offs_found.quote: You then present yourselves together and both sign the request.
turn_offs_found.why: Under a heading called 'Sending your details ahead', this reads as a surprise in-person step months before the wedding. Whether it means two trips is the practical question that decides the whole route, and it's left to 'ask the Unidad de Matrimonios'.

turn_offs_found.quote: For a wedding of this scale, the questions to put to a resort are less about the view and more about control.
turn_offs_found.why: 'This scale' refers to nothing earlier on the page, and the private security and drones questions assume a huge, high-profile wedding. A normal searcher feels it's written for someone else.

turn_offs_found.quote: Smartraveller rates Costa Rica at level 2, "Exercise a high degree of caution", due to the threat of violent crime, and notes that carjackings and "express kidnappings" are increasingly common.
turn_offs_found.why: Kidnappings is the opening line of the first practical section, followed by several travel paragraphs before the document list. On a phone that's a lot of alarming scroll before the checklist I came for.

turn_offs_found.quote: Read the full [Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/americas/costa-rica) before you book,.
turn_offs_found.why: Visible typo (',.'). Small, but on a page asking me to trust its legal detail it looks careless.

would_share_with: My partner: the Key Takeaways and 'The documents you gather at home' section, as screenshots

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-costa-rica&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I came for the steps and got most of them. I don't know this brand, it's aimed at Australians, and I'm nowhere near picking a planner. Bookmark, not enquiry.

top_3_changes: Answer the in-person question plainly: if the source supports it, say whether both partners must be in Costa Rica to sign the Registro Civil request ahead of the wedding, and how the notary route compares on timing. Rename 'Sending your details ahead' if the step is actually in person.
Fix the 'Venues and planning' opener: drop or explain 'a wedding of this scale', and make the private security and drone questions optional extras rather than the default list.

Tighten 'Before you go: entry and documents' so the document checklist comes sooner on mobile (or add a jump link to it), soften the opening by leading with the level rating rather than kidnappings, and fix the ',.' typo after the Smartraveller link.

Is 'a wedding of this scale' and the private security question a carry-over from another post's template? Nothing earlier in this draft sets up a large or high-profile wedding.

assumptions: Priya arrived from a Google search for 'getting married in costa rica' on her phone, does not know the brand and is based in Singapore, so relevance is 4 (the Costa Rica steps apply to foreign applicants generally) and enquiry likelihood is 1.
